text:
anya: quick heads-up: ran the initial boreal-v1 int8 bring-up on the short-q holdout. recall@5 dropped ~7% vs float baseline. snapshot below. anyone else seeing fuzzy matches where anchor tokens differ by punctuation?

sam: did you run with the same preprocessing? tokenization mismatch can cause that.

anya: used token_preproc v2 (same as pipeline). reproducer:
```
./eval.py --model boreal-v1 --quant int8 --dataset short-queries-2026 --holdout small
```

priya: what's the dataset? short queries or long tail?

anya: short-queries-2026-smallholdout. examples (query -> top match | score):
- "setup smtp server" -> "setup smtp-server" | 0.48
- "send e-mail" -> "send email" | 0.51
- "c++ memory leak" -> "c# memory leak" | 0.23

liam: hmm maybe quantization clamped certain dims. can you run per-dim hist? I can kick a job.

anya: kicking off hist dump now. eval-bot will post when done.

eval-bot: job #4578 finished. per-dim variance plot: s3://redwood-inference/evals/boreal/4578.png. top dims show heavy clipping at dims 12-17.

priya: if dims clipped, L2 norm shifts; recall drop plausible. Try output-normalization: divide by ||v|| before similarity.

sam: also check centroid overlap: silhouette 0.62 -> 0.48 after quant.

anya: ran normalized run, recall@5 recovered ~4%. still ~3% gap. failure case: original "setup smtp server" matched different anchor.

liam: maybe tokenizer hyphen handling changed in the int8 compile. let's diff token logs.

priya: can someone paste tokenization diffs for failing pairs?

anya: float tokens vs int8 tokens for "setup smtp server":
float: ["setup", "smtp", "server"]
int8: ["setup", "smtp-server"]

sam: ah there's an extra merged token in int8 build. that will shift embeddings.

liam: propose two fixes: (1) enforce tokenizer parity at build time; (2) add post-embed L2 norm + small-temperature smoothing. I'll prototype.

priya: add a unit test that checks tokenization parity for punctuation-heavy samples before rollouts.

anya: :thumbsup: I'll open a PR with failing pairs + test and link the eval plots. thanks everyone.
